item: 1.34 — LaTeX math in replies: $$…$$ and \[…\] as display math, \(…\) and $…$ inline, drawn by the vendored KaTeX; money, code and unparseable formulas stay text (2026-11-22)
branch: js/20-markdown.js mathOut (one pass after fenced code is lifted: code spans returned untouched, each formula swapped for a token, tokens put back as KaTeX's HTML in .math / .math.math-d after the blocks are built) · mathHtml (escaped text unescaped for KaTeX, cached, null on a parse error or when window.katex is absent) · css/30-blocks.css .math-d · the page's VENDOR_CSS / VENDOR_JS blocks (WebviewAssets.vendorCss / vendorJs, pinned by WebviewVendorTest)
provenance: No wire frames: math is the panel's own rendering of reply text, driven through renderMd — the one function live streaming, replay, plan cards, side answers and bookmarks all draw through. The delimiters are the four VS Code 2.1.330 renders (its CHANGELOG line and the audit, 2026-11-22); KaTeX 0.19.1 is the npm package's dist, unchanged. The library was the user's pick the same day from three candidates rendered side by side in the real panel (KaTeX with its fonts, Temml on native MathML, KaTeX's MathML output): the browser's own MathML layout left brackets unstretched and sums cramped. The font check reads document.fonts for a KaTeX face, which only passes when the inlined data: URIs really loaded. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN 2026-11-22 against the pre-change webview (the sandbox on f7e5e94, `typeof mathOut` 'undefined'; window.katex WAS defined there, left over from the candidates render, so the control isolates the renderer change): 17 passed / 16 failed — every DISCRIMINATING assert, plus the sideways-scroll guard that needs a .math-d to exist.
